sentences.text: P.S. TO JUDGE PJ  A.M.SHAFFIQUE, J

----------------------------------------
 Dated this the 26th day of May 2014  J U D G M E N T Petitioner has approached this Court seeking a direction to the 1st respondent to order release of the goods covered under Ext.P6.
2.
The facts involved in the above case would disclose that the petitioner imported 132 bags of fermented and dried Coco Beans and certain other items under Ext.P6 Bill of Entry.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), on inspection, found that coco beans were contaminated with fungal growth.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the prescribed standards, the materials should be free from fungus.
Ext.P7 is the report of the FSSAI which was communicated to the petitioner as well.
According to the petitioner, after necessary fumigation, the fungal growth would be wiped off and there is no reason for detaining the goods.

3. In fact, pursuant to Ext.P7, the goods were not permitted to be released to the petitioner and it will be either confiscated or destroyed or necessary permission would be granted to re-export the materials, if it is permissible as per the procedure prescribed.
4. Counter affidavit is filed by the 1st respondent inter alia stating the measures that are to be taken while importing food products.

It is inter alia stated that import of all edible/ food products including tea, domestic sale and manufacture of which are governed by Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Rules thereunder, shall also be subject to the conditions laid down in the aforesaid Act and Rules framed thereunder and the import of all these products will have to comply with the quality and packaging requirements as laid down in the Act.

As it is indicated that Cocoa Beans comes under `food product', coming within the schedule to the said Act, unless it is cleared by the FSSAI Department, it may not be possible for the petitioner to take release of the goods.

5. Petitioner subsequently produced Ext.P9 to indicate that the Director of Plant Protection,
Quarantine & Storage Department, Government of India has issued certificate dated 13/05/2014 M/S.St.George Industries vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 28 November, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26595297/
3 indicating that the consignment has `passed'.

entities.text: S.St.George Industries vs The Commissioner Of Customs
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact, no specific details are mentioned in Ext.P9.
At any rate, if the Customs wants to clear the goods aforesaid, necessary permission from the FSSAI is required, which is a mandatory provision.
Under these circumstances, I do not think that Ext.P9 will render any assistance to the petitioner.
Having regard to the aforesaid factual circumstances, there is no reason to permit release of the aforesaid goods to the petitioner and accordingly the writ petition is dismissed.
However, with liberty to the petitioner to approach the respondent authority seeking for re-export, if it is permissible as per the procedure prescribed.
